title: The Devil is in the Spectrum: Mitigating Representation Collapse in LLMs via Topologically Regularized Side-Path
claim: Standard attention collapses into over-mixed or isolated patterns across similarity, operator and topology views; ours yields a balanced, non-degenerate structure.
layout: 3 stacked rows (a-c), left pathologies vs right 'ours' column, dashed divider
description: A three-row figure split by a vertical dashed line. The left side shows pathologies, and the right column in red 'TRSP (ours)' shows the fix. Row (a) shows token-similarity heatmaps S. Homogenization collapse is a uniformly gray matrix. Isolation collapse has only a sharp diagonal. Ours has a soft banded diagonal. Row (b) shows blue transition-operator heatmaps M. Over-mixing is uniform, attention sink has a dark first column plus a diagonal, and local attention is diagonal only. Ours is a smooth diagonal band. Row (c) shows token graphs from X_in to X_out. The fully-connected, star and disconnected graphs sit on gray panels. Ours has two dense clusters joined by a few cross links. Equations sit under the titles, and the red labels draw the eye first.
caption: Analysis of representation collapse. (a) Token Similarity S. Attention may degenerate into homogenization collapse (indistinguishable tokens) or isolation collapse (context failure). (b) Transition Operator M. Homogenization may stem from overmixing or an attention sink, while isolation arises from local attention. (c) Topological Connectivity. These pathologies originate from fully connected/centralized star graphs versus disconnected graphs, respectively. By applying spectrally guided topology regularization, our approach constructs a non-degenerate transition operator M that effectively mitigates representation collapse.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are fundamentally limited by representation collapse, a bottleneck that severely degrades long-context performance. We identify that existing approaches risk drifting into one of two pathological extremes: homogenization collapse (e.g., attention sinks causing rank deficiency) and isolation collapse (e.g., local attention causing context disconnection). Through spectral analysis of attention dynamics, we derive an intrinsic trade-off between mixing efficiency (spectral gap) and information capacity (effective rank) that standard mechanisms struggle to balance. To resolve this dilemma, we propose the Topologically Regularized Side-Path (TRSP), a non-invasive architectural intervention that achieves spectral balance. TRSP employs a parameter-free Triangular Box mechanism, scaled by a lightweight, length-aware gate, to regularize the token interaction topology. By integrating proximal coupling to preserve effective rank and distal propagation to support non-degenerate mixing, TRSP promotes a geometrically healthier transition operator without altering core attention. Experiments show significant improvements across general capabilities and long-context benchmarks. Notably, on NoLiMa at $8\times$ the training length, TRSP retains $83\%$ accuracy and surpasses the Differential Transformer and Gated Attention by approximately 30 and 50 percentage points, respectively. Code available at: https://github.com/Eziotao-tyd/TRSP.
